INDEPENDENT REFERENCE for this epic acceptance criterion: "Across deterministic Monte Carlo replications, null estimates center at zero and planted effects recover the declared conditional target within a prespecified Monte Carlo error."

Built in pure base R, importing no package code. Establishes the target, the tolerance, and - most importantly - evidence that the criterion actually discriminates.

Setup: n=120, q=4 conditions, p=30 features, R=6 runs, block design, contrast c = (1,-1,0,0). Spatially correlated noise Sigma = A^T A / p + 0.5 I. Planted effect on the contrast direction. Estimator is the ordered-pair crossvalidated Mahalanobis form, mean over a != b of delta_a Sigma^-1 delta_b^T, which matches the tr[(c c^T) B_a K B_b^T] form this epic evaluates with a supplied true precision.

  true squared Mahalanobis target : 3.728339
  NULL    mean = +0.003071   MC se = 0.004899   z = +0.63
  SIGNAL  mean = +3.714054   MC se = 0.020777   bias = -0.014284   z(bias) = -0.69

Both are unbiased at 400 replications: the null sits 0.63 standard errors from zero, the signal 0.69 standard errors from the target.

PRESPECIFIED TOLERANCES you can adopt directly, 3 x MC se at nrep = 400:
  null    |mean| < 0.01470
  signal  |mean - target| < 0.06233
MC se scales as 1/sqrt(nrep): expect ~0.0098 at 100 replications, ~0.0031 at 1000. Choose nrep from the tolerance you want rather than picking a round number.

THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST - the criterion discriminates. The same simulation with the NON-crossvalidated estimator (delta Sigma^-1 delta^T on a single run) gives under the null:

  mean = +1.9725   instead of 0

That is roughly 400 MC standard errors away. So a null-centering test at this tolerance would catch a silently non-crossvalidated implementation immediately. A recovery test that passes for both the correct and the broken estimator would be worthless; this one does not.

Suggestion: assert BOTH arms. Null centering alone is the sensitive one, but signal recovery is what rules out an estimator that is unbiased under the null and wrongly scaled under signal.

Script is reproducible with set.seed(2026); happy to hand it over if useful.
